points.en: darker, greyer crown than the mantle

art.subject: Sakhalin Leaf Warbler (Phylloscopus borealoides), adult (sexes alike), as seen on Korean islands on spring passage: crown and nape greyish-olive, slightly greyer than the olive-brown mantle and wings; long whitish supercilium reaching well behind the eye and a dark eye-stripe; one or two thin pale wing-bars on the coverts; underparts whitish with a greyish-buff wash on the flanks. Bill with a dark upper mandible and a pale pinkish lower mandible; dark eye; legs and feet pale pink.
art.pose: foraging low in shaded undergrowth, pumping its tail downward
art.scene: shady broadleaf woodland on a Korean offshore island in May, fresh green leaves and dappled light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view foraging low on a shaded branch, tail dipped downward: slim leaf warbler, darker, greyer crown than the brownish-olive mantle and wings, long broad whitish supercilium, broad dark eye-stripe, pale ear-coverts, whitish underparts, pale pinkish legs and feet

adult, front three-quarter view perched low on a mossy rock: long whitish supercilium, broad dark eye-stripe, pale ear-coverts, darker grey crown, whitish throat and breast, pale pinkish legs and feet
art.build: Small leaf warbler, smaller than a tree sparrow, slim with a fairly long, slender bill and a medium-length tail. Legs pale pink and rather strong-looking for a leaf warbler. Forages low in shady undergrowth and on lower branches, frequently pumping its tail downward.
avoid: Do not paint dark legs (Arctic Warbler, Hume's Leaf Warbler); the legs are pale pink.
Do not paint a pale central crown stripe and a yellowish undertail; that is Eastern Crowned Warbler (Phylloscopus coronatus).
Do not paint bright green upperparts, yellow underparts or bold wing-bars.
